list

List entities by kind.

Usage:
  agent-issues list <kind> [--status <comma-separated statuses>] [--parent <id>] [--limit <count>]

Arguments:
  kind | Entity kind. | required | allowed: project, epic, version, initiative, prd, userStory, adr, issue, debt, handoff, plan

Options:
  --status <comma-separated statuses> | Include only entities with a selected status. | allowed: active, approved, archived, blocked, current, deferred, done, draft, in-progress, open, paused, ready, resolved, superseded, todo
  --parent <id> | Include only entities with this structural parent.
  --limit <count> | Return at most this many entities. Total reports the full filtered count.
  --db <path> | Use a specific SQLite database path.
  --json | Print machine-readable JSON. Entity mutations return acknowledgements; list and relation reads return summaries.
  --pretty | Pretty-print JSON when used with --json.
  --help, -h | Show help for the whole CLI or the selected command.

Examples:
  agent-issues list issue
  agent-issues list issue --status todo,in-progress --parent <initiativeId> --limit 20 --json
  agent-issues list debt --status open --json

Notes:
  JSON returns { items, total }; total is the filtered count before --limit is applied.
  Use --status, --parent, and --limit to select records before serialization.
  Accepted status values depend on the entity kind; use agent-issues schema --json to inspect each kind's workflow.
  For kind=issue, JSON also returns openBlockers: an entityId -> open (not-done) blocking issue ids map, so a candidate's blocked status is visible without a separate relations call per issue.

Output:
  Human-readable:
    One line per entity: <id> <status> <title>
    Issue lines append (blocked by <id>, ...) when openBlockers is non-empty.
  JSON fields:
    { items: CompactEntity[], total: number, openBlockers?: Record<string, string[]> }
